hints: Let X be the number of attempts up to and including Rajesh's first success: X ~ Geo(0.3).
Success for the first time on the 7th attempt requires 6 consecutive failures followed by 1 success.
walkthrough:
Model the number of attempts until the first success as a Geometric distribution with $p = 0.3$ and $q = 0.7$:
$$X \sim \operatorname{Geo}(0.3)$$
$$P(X = 7) = (1 - p)^6 p = (0.7)^6 (0.3)$$

Evaluate the power and find the probability:
$$P(X = 7) = 0.117649 \times 0.3 = 0.0352947 \approx 0.0353$$
$$(0.0352 \le p \le 0.0353)$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the probability model and its parameter:
Rajesh applies each year independently with constant success probability $p = 0.3$.
The number of attempts $X$ until his first success follows a Geometric distribution:
$$X \sim \operatorname{Geo}(p) = \operatorname{Geo}(0.3)$$
where failure probability on any attempt is $q = 1 - p = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7$.

Step 2: State the geometric probability mass function:
$$P(X = r) = q^{r-1} p = (1 - p)^{r-1} p$$

Step 4: Compute the numerical value:
$$(0.7)^6 = 0.117649$$
$$P(X = 7) = 0.117649 \times 0.3 = 0.0352947 \approx 0.0353$$
(To 3 significant figures).

hints: Being successful for the first time before the 6th attempt means the first success occurs on attempts 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5: P(X <= 5).
Use the cumulative geometric formula: P(X <= k) = 1 - (1 - p)^k.
walkthrough:
Apply the cumulative distribution formula $P(X \le k) = 1 - (1 - p)^k$ with $k = 5$ and $1 - p = 0.7$:
$$P(X \le 5) = 1 - (0.7)^5 = 1 - 0.16807 = 0.83193 \approx 0.832$$
$$(0.8319 \le p \le 0.832)$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand the required event:
For $X \sim \operatorname{Geo}(0.3)$, success before the 6th attempt means that the first success occurs on attempt $1, 2, 3, 4,$ or $5$:
$$P(X < 6) = P(X \le 5)$$

Step 2: Apply the complement of failing the first 5 attempts:
The only way the first success does NOT occur on or before attempt $5$ is if Rajesh fails all $5$ of his first $5$ attempts:
$$P(X \le 5) = 1 - P(\text{fails first } 5 \text{ attempts}) = 1 - q^5$$

Step 3: Substitute the failure probability q = 0.7:
$$P(X \le 5) = 1 - (0.7)^5$$

Step 4: Evaluate the power and subtract:
$$(0.7)^5 = 0.16807$$
$$P(X \le 5) = 1 - 0.16807 = 0.83193 \approx 0.832$$
(To 3 significant figures).

hints: For the second success to happen on the 10th attempt, two conditions must occur.
First, Rajesh must have exactly 1 success in his first 9 attempts: 9C1 * (0.3)^1 * (0.7)^8.
Second, Rajesh must be successful on his 10th attempt with probability 0.3.
walkthrough:
Decompose the event of second success on the 10th attempt into two independent events:
1. Exactly $1$ success in the first $9$ attempts: $\binom{9}{1} (0.3)^1 (0.7)^8$
2. Success on the $10$th attempt: $0.3$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand the structure of the kth success on the rth trial:
For Rajesh to achieve his second success on his 10th attempt, the following two conditions must both be satisfied:
1. In his first $9$ attempts, he must succeed exactly once (and fail $8$ times).
2. On his 10th attempt, he must succeed.

Step 2: Calculate the probability of exactly 1 success in the first 9 attempts:
Using the Binomial probability formula for $n = 9, r = 1, p = 0.3, q = 0.7$:
$$P(1 \text{ success in } 9) = \binom{9}{1} (0.3)^1 (0.7)^8 = 9 \times 0.3 \times (0.7)^8$$

Step 3: Multiply by the probability of success on the 10th attempt:
$$P = P(1 \text{ success in } 9) \times P(\text{success on 10th})$$
$$P = 9 \times 0.3 \times (0.7)^8 \times 0.3 = 9 \times (0.3)^2 \times (0.7)^8$$

Step 4: Compute the numerical value:
$$(0.3)^2 = 0.09$$
$$(0.7)^8 = 0.05764801$$
$$P = 9 \times 0.09 \times 0.05764801 = 0.81 \times 0.05764801 = 0.046694888... \approx 0.0467$$
(To 3 significant figures).
